Thanks again for the demo last week. As we evaluate Redwood for a multi-phase deployment across our lending products, procurement has asked us to submit the attached RFI focusing on staged adoption, connectivity, and rollback controls.

Can you and your team complete the questionnaire and provide a recommended staging cadence (pilot -> canary -> regional ramp) and the minimal infra/network requirements per phase? We're particularly sensitive to data residency, audit trails, and an air-gapped fallback for our highest-risk workflows.

I've attached the RFI PDF and put the baseline integration doc in the shared Drive (link below). We'd like your responses by EOD Tuesday (13 Apr) to align with our vendor scorecard.

Rachel — thanks for the packet and the timeline. We're on it. Quick notes up-front:

- We'll fill out the questionnaire and return a detailed staged cadence proposal. Recommended target: two-week pilot (non-prod), 1-week canary (limited live traffic), then 4-week regional ramp, with a final global cutover scheduled no earlier than 8 weeks after pilot depending on validation metrics.
- We will include both hosted (Redwood API) and Private (VPC) deployment options with explicit failure-mode behavior for each phase.
- Data residency: we can lock model execution to specific regions and provide event-level audit logs for every inference request.

I'll have a first draft by end of day Monday. Markus will add the fallback runbook for the Private deployment variant.

Two quick asks for your Ops team:
1) Can you confirm the outbound IP allowlist window for the pilot?
2) Do you require encrypted transit on an IPsec tunnel or will TLS with mTLS be sufficient for the pilot phase?

Hi Rachel, Kim —

Attached is the staged adoption runbook draft and a compact connectivity checklist for your DevOps review. Highlights:

- Pilot (2 weeks, non-prod): use Redwood Hosted API with per-tenant prefix caching enabled. Minimum: 2 reserved inference vCPU equivalents (we'll size GPU capacity on our side) and a small test dataset of representative prompts. Expected latency baseline: p95 < 180ms.

- Canary (1 week, 5-10% live traffic): shift to Dedicated pool with a pinned model variant (intel-8bit quant). Autoscaler set with conservative headroom. Add request-level tracing and sample output snapshots to your S3 bucket for validation.

- Regional ramp (4 weeks/stage): expand percentage and add A/B quality comparisons. Thresholds: automated rollback if quality drift > 3% on cosine-sim eval or error-rate spike > 1.5x baseline.

- Fallbacks: Immediate fallback to a smaller model variant + traffic shedding policy. For Private deployments we include a pre-configured offline model artifact and an air-gap ingestion path for high-sensitivity workflows.

Security/connectivity options:
- TLS + mTLS is sufficient for the pilot if you can rotate certs every 90 days. For regulated workloads we recommend an IPsec site-to-site tunnel into your VPC and we support HSM-backed key wrap for model encryption.

I left inline comments in the attached doc (redwood-staged-adoption-runbook-v1.docx).

Regards,
Markus

Attachment: redwood-staged-adoption-runbook-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our DevOps review:

1) The pilot will run inside our non-prod VPC but traffic will originate from a set of managed test runners. We can provide an ephemeral allowlist, but would prefer mTLS over IPsec initially.
2) For the canary, we need a way to mute sampling of PII in the sample snapshots before they land in our S3 tenant. Can you outline the sanitization hooks or shims?

Also, procurement asked that you confirm whether Redwood can provide SOC2 Type II evidence for the Dedicated environment and whether audit logs can be retained for 12 months (we may request 24 months for some workflows).

Can you respond to the bullet items and update the runbook with a short table that maps phase -> required Orbit-owned network changes?

Best,
Rachel

Rachel — following up with the updated materials. I've attached a short appendix that addresses PII sanitization, SOC2 evidence availability, and the per-phase network change table you requested. Summary answers below:

- mTLS: supported for pilot (we supply client certs via short-lived PKI; rotation policy documented).
- PII sanitization: we provide a pre-ingest sanitizer that masks tokens and common PII patterns; for canary snapshots you'll be able to toggle redaction rules and run a verification pass before export. Implementation notes are in Appendix A.
- SOC2 Type II: Redwood can share a redacted SOC2 Type II report for our Dedicated environment under an NDA. Audit logs: configurable retention up to 24 months for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers (12 months default for hosted tiers).

I've also added the phase->network-change table and a short backout checklist for each stage. Please see the Drive link for the consolidated package; I've pushed a signed DocuSign for the NDA which will unlock the SOC2 artifact.

Attachments: appendix-a-pii-sanitization.pdf (application/pdf)

Let us know if you want a quick run-through (30 min) tomorrow to validate the runbook.

Thanks,
